name: space-rows-switch-spaces
description:
the palette offered a New Space verb and no way to reach a space that already exists. The snapshot carried tabs and favourites and nothing about spaces, so a user who knew the name of the space they wanted had to leave the palette to get there.

The fixture holds two spaces, 'Daylight' active and 'Zephyr' beside it, one tab each. 'zeph' is the measurement text: it is in no tab title, in no host, in no favourite and in none of the local verbs' keywords, so a space row is the only Atrium row the query can produce. That is what makes the count assertion below mean 'the space producer answered' rather than 'something answered'.

Return then takes that row while it is the top one. The vlog line names BOTH ends of the move and the destination space by name, so a run that switched nowhere, or switched to the space it was already in, cannot satisfy it.

What is NOT claimed: the palette does not rank spaces, it filters them - two spaces matching 'zeph' would both be offered, in rail order. The empty query is covered by the unit test rather than here, because the interesting half of it (no space rows before a key is pressed) is a negative that this window's tab rows would mask.

actions.note: GATE: the active space's tab has committed, so the sidebar model is built
the reserved chrome context lands about 670ms after startup and the palette's WebContents needs it
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
let the /commandbar document commit and take the field
the pass answering 'zeph' lands with the autocomplete one
one space row, glyph and 'Space' label before the omnibox rows
How many spaces the typed text offers
which space it is, read through a different query than the count
and it is the row Return is about to take, so the assertion below is about this row

assertions.desc: 'zeph' names one space and nothing else in this window, so the palette offers exactly that row
the row carries the space's name from the sidebar model, so the count above is not one of something else
the space row is highlighted, which is what makes the Return below act on it rather than on an omnibox row

assertions.label: space-row-accept-switched-spaces
assertions.desc: Return on a space row reached SelectSpace, from the space the fixture starts in to the one the row names. Nothing at launch logs this - the fixture's active space is already 0, and no snoozed tab wakes here.
